# Ontario Landlord-Tenant Dispute Prep Checklist

Your goal is to build a clean paper trail, understand the landlord’s claim, and be ready to speak with the Landlord and Tenant Board or a lawyer. I’ll keep this practical and non-definitive.

## What to Gather Before You Respond

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- Lease agreement and any renewals or amendments
- Your written notice dated **2025-04-15**
- Proof the notice was delivered and received
- Rent payment history and receipts
- Any messages with the landlord about move-out, re-renting, or extra rent
- Move-out condition photos/videos with timestamps
- Keys returned record, if any
- Any listing screenshots or ads showing when the unit was re-listed
- Any written demand from the landlord for the extra month
- Notes of phone calls, including dates, times, and what was said

## Questions to Ask the Tenancy Board or a Lawyer

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

- Was my notice to end the tenancy valid for the date I gave?
- Does the landlord have to prove actual loss or a legal basis for the extra month?
- What notice period applies to my tenancy type and lease terms?
- Does the landlord have a duty to mitigate by trying to re-rent?
- What evidence would matter most if this goes to a hearing?
- Should I pay anything now, or wait for a formal claim?
- If I disagree, what is the safest way to respond in writing?
- What deadlines apply if the landlord files an application or demand?

## Calm Response Letter Draft

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/file-earmark-text.svg

Use a short, neutral tone and avoid arguing the law in the first message.

- State the facts: you gave written notice on **2025-04-15** to end the tenancy on **2025-06-30**
- Say you understand the landlord is asking for one extra month
- Ask for the request in writing, with the reason and supporting documents
- Ask for a breakdown of the amount claimed
- Say you are reviewing the issue and will respond after obtaining advice
- Keep the tone respectful and non-admitting

Suggested wording:
“Thank you for your message. I gave written notice on 2025-04-15 to end my tenancy on 2025-06-30. I understand you are requesting an additional month of rent because the unit was not re-rented immediately. Please send your request in writing, along with the basis for the amount claimed and any supporting documents. I am reviewing the matter and will respond after I have had a chance to obtain advice.”

## Practical Next Steps

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

- Save everything in one folder, both PDF and screenshots
- Make a timeline with dates, messages, and events
- Do not delete texts, emails, or listing evidence
- If you speak by phone, follow up by email the same day
- Keep all replies brief, factual, and polite
- If money is demanded, ask for a written itemization before paying

## Sources

- Landlord and Tenant Board: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Tribunals Ontario forms and guides: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms/
- Government of Ontario housing information: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario
